allowed_alternatives: A formal two-sample t-test or Welch's test comparing the pooled recipe samples (n=45) against the baseline population (n=60) to explicitly verify that the observed >1 HRC difference completely dwarfs any plausible sampling error.
evidence: Baseline mean 58.182 HRC, standard deviation 0.741 HRC (n=60).
Recipe means: A = 59.102, B = 59.311, C = 59.327 (n=15 each, pooled mean ~59.25).

The gap between the baseline mean and the pooled recipes mean is ~1.07 HRC. With pooled standard errors, this represents a difference of more than 7 standard errors, rendering the report's claim that it is 'consistent with sampling' mathematically impossible.
The report asserts: 'that gap is consistent with sampling and the baseline's skew, not with a recipe effect.'
reviews.rationale: The report correctly recognizes the lack of a statistically significant difference among the three heat-treat recipes. However, it catastrophically misinterprets the massive, >7 standard error shift between the baseline samples (~58.2 HRC) and the experimental recipe samples (~59.25 HRC). It falsely dismisses this highly significant >1 HRC shift as 'consistent with sampling and baseline's skew' without performing any formal test. Even worse, the report recommends holding the process to the baseline's control chart (CL=58.182)—a chart on which the recent recipe process would practically trigger a continuous out-of-control signal, as nearly all of its output is above the centerline. Closing an investigation while actively ignoring a massive, systemic process shift is fundamentally invalid and professionally unacceptable in industrial practice.
reviews.numerical_check: Calculated the standard error of the baseline mean (0.741/sqrt(60) = 0.096) and the pooled recipes mean (approx 0.66/sqrt(45) = 0.098), yielding a standard error of the difference of ~0.137. The ~1.07 HRC difference is therefore >7.7 standard errors apart (p < 0.00001). Furthermore, the baseline's right-skew actually means the median is lower than the mean, so using medians would reveal an even larger shift than using means, directly refuting the report's justification.
